summary_en: Full-year dividend per share raised to 10 yen from 5 yen, with year-end payout doubled to 10 yen. Upgrade reflects better-than-expected H1 results driven by higher-margin product mix, price corrections, and cost controls despite challenging automotive sector conditions.
title_en: Notice Regarding Differences Between FY2027 Q2 Earnings Forecasts and Actual Results, Revision of Full-Year Earnings Forecasts, and Revision of Dividend Forecasts (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Nippon Kinzoku has raised its full-year dividend forecast to 10 yen per share from the previously announced 5 yen. The year-end dividend has been doubled to 10 yen, with no interim dividend. This revision reflects better-than-expected first-half results, where the company exceeded consolidated operating profit and attributable profit forecasts.

Despite challenging conditions in its core automotive sector, with some softening in overseas sales, the company achieved strong H1 performance through three main drivers: shifting product mix toward higher-margin items, adjusting sales prices to reflect cost increases, and aggressively reducing operational costs including selling, general and administrative expenses. These initiatives resulted in H1 consolidated operating profit of 772 million yen against a 630 million yen forecast, and attributable profit of 446 million yen against 230 million yen expected.

Based on this H1 outperformance and revised full-year earnings guidance, consolidated profit attributable to parent company shareholders for fiscal year ending March 2027 was raised to 620 million yen from 510 million yen. While management acknowledges ongoing risks including further cost pressures in Q3-Q4 and global economic headwinds, the improved earnings trajectory supports the higher dividend payout.
